title: AdamMeme: Adaptively Probe the Reasoning Capacity of Multimodal Large Language Models on Harmfulness

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating mLLMs' ability to detect and explain harmfulness in memes containing racial stereotypes, anti-Black bias, and dehumanization, using an iterative agent-based framework that modifies meme text to create more challenging, nuanced samples and scores the model's reasoning.

Assessing models on deciphering memes that perpetuate gender stereotypes, misogyny, and objectification through adaptive meme text refinement and LLM-as-a-judge scoring of the models' generated explanations.

Testing the target models' capacity to identify intolerance, misrepresentation of religious beliefs, or hatred (e.g., Islamophobia) using dynamically modified multimodal memes and multi-agent evaluation.

Probing mLLMs' understanding of xenophobia and national stereotypes by iteratively refining meme texts to obscure explicit harmful cues and scoring the models' ability to identify the underlying prejudice.

Evaluating model responses to memes that mock, belittle, or stereotype individuals with physical or mental disabilities, utilizing an adaptive evaluation loop to expose model-specific weaknesses in recognizing nuanced harm.
Measuring models' recognition of divisive rhetoric, extremism, and harmful stereotypes directed at political groups or figures using agent-generated challenging meme variations.
